definitions.explanation: In karate and several other martial arts, paired training or competition in which two practitioners exchange techniques. Contrasted with solo {型|かた} (forms) practice.

examples.japanese: {組|く}み{手|て}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{練習|れんしゅう}→練習：05323_renshuu⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦する→する：00392_suru⟧。

⟦{空手|からて}→空手：04454_karate⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{試合|しあい}→試合：01601_shiai⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{型|かた}→型：02146_kata⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧{組|く}み{手|て}⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{二|ふた}つ→二つ：02953_futatsu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{部門|ぶもん}→部門：14406_bumon⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{分|わ}かれている→分かれる：10976_wakareru⟧。
examples.english: Karate competitions are divided into two divisions: forms and sparring.

notes:
From ⟦{組|く}む→組む：02050_kumu⟧ (to join, to engage) + ⟦{手|て}→手：00569_te⟧ (hand). The image is two opponents 'joining hands' — engaging each other in technique exchange.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {組|く}み{手|て}{試合|じあい}: a sparring match
- ⟦{自由|じゆう}→自由：01148_jiyuu⟧{組|く}み{手|て}: free sparring (unscripted)
- ⟦{約束|やくそく}→約束：01517_yakusoku⟧{組|く}み{手|て}: prearranged sparring (set sequence)

USAGE:
Most strongly associated with karate, where competition is split into ⟦{型|かた}→型：02146_kata⟧ (kata, solo forms) and {組|く}み{手|て} (kumite, sparring). Also used in ⟦{柔道|じゅうどう}→柔道：01612_juudou⟧, ⟦{合気道|あいきどう}→合気道：17630_aikidou⟧, and other arts. Both 'kata' and 'kumite' are used as loanwords in English-speaking martial arts communities.
